name: vLLM
summary: A model-serving runtime that schedules variable-length generation requests, manages attention KV memory with paged blocks, supports distributed execution, and exposes OpenAI-compatible and other service APIs.

features.name: Continuous batching request scheduler
features.description: vLLM's serving engine admits and schedules concurrent generation requests, including continuous batching and chunked prefill, so active requests can share execution steps while having different sequence lengths.
benefits: Improves utilization opportunities for mixed request arrivals
Makes admission and iteration scheduling explicit runtime responsibilities
costs: Scheduling policy and queue state affect latency and fairness
Variable request shapes increase coordination and memory-management complexity

features.name: PagedAttention KV-cache management
features.description: vLLM manages attention key/value cache storage in blocks rather than requiring each sequence to occupy one contiguous allocation, and its PagedAttention design is a central serving abstraction.
benefits: Reduces dependence on contiguous per-sequence cache allocations
Allows cache blocks to be scheduled and reused as request state changes
costs: Block tables and allocation policy add runtime metadata and indirection
Cache capacity, eviction, and sharing semantics remain workload-dependent

features.name: Parallel and distributed model execution
features.description: The project supports tensor, pipeline, data, expert, and context parallelism plus multiple hardware backends, making execution placement a configurable boundary around model workers.
benefits: Maps large models and workload replicas onto multiple devices or processes
Separates model execution topology from the client API
costs: Collective communication and topology choices become correctness and operations concerns
Supported features differ across hardware and model architectures

features.name: OpenAI-compatible and multi-protocol serving boundary
features.description: vLLM provides an API server compatible with OpenAI-style clients and documents additional Anthropic Messages and gRPC interfaces, exposing model execution through process-level request and streaming protocols.
benefits: Allows existing client contracts to target the serving runtime
Separates transport, request validation, and scheduling from model kernels
costs: Protocol compatibility does not guarantee identical model or sampling semantics
The server adds lifecycle, authentication, and deployment concerns outside the engine core

mathematical_views.question: How can requests with different arrival times and sequence lengths share iterative model execution?
assumptions: A scheduler state records waiting, running, prefill, and decode work
Each iteration respects request token and resource constraints
The view abstracts kernel-specific execution costs

mathematical_views.question: Which cache-block assignments represent active sequence prefixes and how can they change without copying an entire contiguous cache?
assumptions: A sequence maps logical positions to physical cache blocks
Block allocation and reclamation preserve the sequence's attention state
This is a structural model and not a performance guarantee

mathematical_views.question: Under what topology and collective-communication assumptions can model partitions compose into one request-level result?
assumptions: Communication and synchronization boundaries are explicit
The view does not claim fault tolerance or equal performance

benefits: Shares iterative execution across changing request sets
Flexible cache allocation for variable sequences
costs: Block metadata and cache policy overhead
